name: Hyperscaler-bundled feature platforms
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Six hyperscaler-bundled feature platforms define this segment as of May 2026. (1) Databricks Data Intelligence Platform / Lakebase / Agent Bricks - the runaway leader after two consecutive acquisitions: Fennel (Apr 17 2025, Rust-based incremental compute engine, customers Upwork/Cricut/marketplace recsys) and Tecton (Aug 22 2025, ~$900M deal, sub-10ms latency / sub-100ms freshness / 99.99% uptime, ~$100M ARR at acquisition, Coinbase/Plaid/JPMC reference customers); plus the Lakebase managed-Postgres OLTP layer (launched Jun 11 2025) which now backs Databricks Online Feature Stores as the underlying autoscaling Postgres store, plus MosaicML/MLflow already in the stack. Databricks reached ~$3.7B ARR in 2025 with AI products at a $1.4B Q4-2025 run-rate (~26% of total revenue) on a $100B valuation. (2) Redis Feature Form - launched Apr 20 2026 after the Featureform acquisition Oct 9 2025; bundles feature definition, orchestration, versioning, governance (workspaces, mTLS, audit logs, RBAC, API key pairs), DAG management, sub-millisecond reads on top of the existing Redis Enterprise online tier. (3) Snowflake Feature Store - Python API in snowflake-ml-python (Snowpark ML), feature views auto-maintained via Snowflake Dynamic Tables with 1-minute minimum target lag (lower in preview), ML Lineage automatic; plus Snowflake's Online Feature Store layer (post-Crunchy Data acquisition Jun 2025, $250M) for lower-latency serving. (4) AWS SageMaker Feature Store - DynamoDB-backed online tier (sub-10ms), S3/Iceberg+Parquet offline tier, official fraud-detection example notebook (sagemaker_featurestore_fraud_detection_python_sdk.ipynb), pricing via storage + API calls + DynamoDB throughput (Atlassian's published $425k/yr -> $40k/yr optimisation story). (5) Vertex AI Feature Store (Google Cloud) - BigQuery offline + dual online options: Optimized Online Serving (~$0.38/node-hr, 99% within 2ms internal benchmark) and Bigtable Online Serving (~$1.20/node-hr, ~30ms server-side at ~100 QPS, ~15k QPS per node, 5TB per node); GA on BigQuery-powered architecture with Dataplex integration; lighthouse customers Wayfair, Shopify. (6) Azure ML Managed Feature Store - GA (April 2024 announcement, multiple GA features by 2025-2026 including custom feature source, international/sovereign regions, offline backfill, bootstrap materialisation), ADLS Gen2 offline + Azure Managed Redis online; plus the cross-bundle Azure Databricks Feature Store option.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Mapped to beava's three referenced use cases (18a online FS for fraud, 18b online FS for recsys, 10 marketplace integrity), the dominant bundle differs by buyer's existing cloud. Databricks owns the fraud/risk lighthouse references via Tecton's prior customer base (Coinbase millisecond withdrawal scoring + sequence-feature framework, Plaid Signal ACH ATO on-demand-feature-views, JPMorgan Chase 9ms p99 Inferentia3 screening, and Tecton's published 0.8ms feature retrieval / 100M txn/day / 40% false-positive-reduction reference) plus the Fennel customer base (Upwork credit-risk, Cricut, marketplace recsys). For recsys/ranking (18b), Vertex AI Feature Store has Wayfair and Shopify as named adopters; SageMaker FS has DoorDash-class workloads serviced via 'roll your own with DynamoDB+ElastiCache' (>1M predictions/sec, >20M feature reads/sec) inside the AWS perimeter; Databricks-now-Tecton is the credible play for Whatnot-class live commerce. For marketplace integrity (10), no hyperscaler bundle has a published seller-velocity / refund-rate / image-reuse case study yet; Riskified, Sift, Forter and Signifyd remain the dominant end-to-end vendors and increasingly run on top of one of these bundles. Redis Feature Form is too new (Apr 2026 launch) to have public per-domain case studies but inherits Redis Enterprise's reference base (DoorDash, Instacart, Swiggy via ElastiCache historically). Funding/M&A: Databricks $100B valuation 2025 / $3.7B ARR; Tecton $900M acquisition Aug 2025; Fennel undisclosed Apr 2025; Featureform undisclosed Oct 2025 (Redis); Snowflake bought Crunchy Data Jun 2025 for $250M and TensorStax Feb 2026; Databricks acquired Neon May 2025 for ~$1B.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Proprietary across the board. Databricks Lakebase / Agent Bricks / Tecton / Fennel are closed-source managed services (Tecton was proprietary SaaS pre-acquisition; both are now Databricks-internal). Snowflake Feature Store + Dynamic Tables are proprietary Snowflake features. SageMaker Feature Store and Vertex AI Feature Store and Azure ML Managed Feature Store are closed-source managed cloud services. Redis Feature Form runs on top of Redis 8 (Redis abandoned its BSD-3 license in Mar 2024 for a dual SSPL/RSAL source-available license, prompting the Valkey fork which AWS/GCP and Ubuntu 26.04 now ship as the default 'redis' package) - meaning Feature Form is effectively source-available-only and is the canonical 'rug-pulled' license posture in this segment. The aggregate posture is 'no Apache-2.0 option exists in the hyperscaler-bundled tier' - which is precisely beava's structural wedge against this segment.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High - by construction, this segment IS the hyperscaler bundling threat. Every entry in this segment is bundled into a hyperscaler subscription the buyer already pays for: Databricks customers get Tecton-backed feature serving and Lakebase Online Feature Stores embedded in Agent Bricks with no separate procurement; Snowflake customers get Feature Store + Dynamic Tables as part of their existing Snowflake contract; AWS customers get SageMaker FS with metered DynamoDB/S3 pass-through pricing; GCP customers get Vertex AI FS bundled with their BigQuery spend; Azure customers get Azure ML Managed Feature Store + Azure Databricks Feature Store as part of their Azure ML estate; Redis Enterprise customers get Feature Form bundled. The buyer-side EU DORA regulation (in force Jan 17 2025, 19 critical ICT third-party providers designated Nov 18 2025 including AWS/Azure/GCP) and EU Data Act (in force Sep 12 2025, mandates cloud-portability) are the *only* meaningful counter-forces. For any buyer who is NOT explicitly avoiding hyperscaler lock-in, the bundled option is the default in 2026 - hence the framing in the task notes that this is the segment beava is most at risk of being commodified out of.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: All six platforms assume hyperscaler-native ingestion. Databricks ingests via Delta Live Tables / Spark Structured Streaming / Auto Loader from Kafka, Kinesis, S3, ADLS, GCS, Event Hubs, plus the Tecton Stream Ingest API and Fennel's incremental compute pipelines; Lakebase is Postgres-protocol so application writes go through the Databricks SDK or pgwire. Snowflake ingests via Snowpipe, Kafka Connector for Snowflake, Snowpipe Streaming, and Dynamic Tables auto-refresh against base tables fed by streaming inserts; on the OLTP side Snowflake-Crunchy Postgres is also pgwire. SageMaker FS ingests via the SageMaker SDK PutRecord API (HTTP), batch ingestion from S3, and Kinesis/Kafka MSK consumers feeding a Lambda PutRecord shim. Vertex AI FS ingests from BigQuery streaming inserts (the offline tier is BigQuery itself), Pub/Sub via Dataflow, plus a streaming write API. Azure ML Managed FS ingests from ADLS Gen2 + offline materialisation jobs; the online tier is Azure Managed Redis. Redis Feature Form ingests via the existing Redis Enterprise client protocol plus its own DAG/orchestration layer. None of these accept beava's HTTP-push or framed-TCP-msgpack mobile-SDK-direct-push pattern without an intermediate Kafka/Kinesis/Pub/Sub broker hop - this is one of the few integration-surface differentiators beava retains.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with the rules-vs-ML coupling tied to the hyperscaler bundle. Databricks pushes the 'Agent Bricks' agentic AI scorer (LLM + tools + Mosaic-trained models) plus MLflow-served XGBoost/LightGBM/PyTorch; the rules-engine path is Lakebase Postgres SQL or Genie-driven. Snowflake couples via Snowpark Python UDFs, Cortex AI for LLM, and Streamlit-in-Snowflake for the rules surface; the scorer can be any UDF-callable model. SageMaker FS feeds SageMaker-hosted endpoints (XGBoost/LightGBM/ONNX/Inferentia/Triton) and AWS Rules Engine / Step Functions on the rules side. Vertex AI FS feeds Vertex AI-hosted models and the Vertex Pipelines DAG. Azure ML FS feeds Azure ML endpoints. Redis Feature Form is scorer-agnostic and explicitly markets itself as the feature substrate under whatever scorer the customer brings. For beava: this means the hyperscaler bundles do not displace the external rules-engine + ML-scorer pattern - they own the path, not the decisioning surface - which leaves an opening for beava as a non-bundled feature substrate that the buyer pairs with their own scorer.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: The single honest framing: Apache-2.0 self-hostable for buyers who refuse hyperscaler lock-in. Five concrete reasons such a buyer would pick beava over any entry in this segment: (1) No hyperscaler dependency - beava is a single Rust binary that runs on commodity Linux, on-prem, in a sovereign-cloud region (AWS European Sovereign Cloud Brandenburg end-2025, Azure Local, Google Cloud Dedicated with Thales France / T-Systems Germany, S3NS SecNumCloud, Microsoft+Delos for German public sector), or in an air-gapped data centre. Every entry in segment X1 either runs in a hyperscaler control plane or requires hyperscaler-owned managed services to function. This is the load-bearing wedge under DORA (in force Jan 17 2025) ICT concentration-risk assessment and EU Data Act (Sep 12 2025) portability requirements - which over 65% of EU financial entities now reportedly fail because they depend on two or more of AWS/Azure/GCP. (2) Apache-2.0 with no open-core upsell and no acquisition risk - beava is the only license-clean option in this segment. Tecton/Fennel/Featureform were all acquired and pulled inside hyperscaler walls in 6 months. Redis Feature Form runs on the post-Mar-2024 SSPL/RSAL Redis 8 stack (the canonical 'rug-pulled' license). (3) Single-binary cost model - no per-node-hour billing ($0.38/$1.20 Vertex AI online serving, ~$0.000125 per DynamoDB RCU at SageMaker scale, Atlassian's published $425k -> $40k optimisation), no minimum spend, no DBU/credit consumption. The cost is the box + the Rust process. (4) Sub-millisecond TCP+msgpack batch_get from the published benchmarks beats Vertex AI Bigtable's ~30ms server-side and is at parity with Tecton's published 0.8ms; on the write side ~684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core covers Sift's amortised ~30k EPS / customer baseline with two orders of magnitude headroom. (5) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives (count, sum, mean, n_unique HLL, CMS top-K, t-digest quantile, velocity, distance, last-N, exponential decays) in the server itself - bundle alternatives all assume upstream Spark/Flink/Dataflow/Beam computes aggregates and writes them to the online store. The buyer trades a streaming-platform-team headcount for a single binary.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps that block adoption against the hyperscaler bundle today: (1) No TLS/auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 in v0 - every hyperscaler bundle ships TLS + IAM + audit logs (Databricks Unity Catalog, SageMaker IAM, Vertex AI IAM, Azure RBAC, Redis Feature Form mTLS + audit logs + API key pairs) out of the box; this is a procurement non-starter for any regulated buyer. SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA / FedRAMP postures all assume authenticated/encrypted endpoints. (2) No multi-region active-active replication - Databricks Online Feature Stores, SageMaker FS, Vertex AI FS, and Azure ML FS all ship cross-region replication; beava in v0 does not. (3) No in-process sharding - the hyperscaler bundles all scale horizontally; beava is single-binary and vertical-only. Databricks Lakebase autoscales, Bigtable adds nodes, DynamoDB autoscales, Snowflake warehouses spin out. (4) No managed offering - the hyperscaler bundles are managed services by definition; beava ships as a self-hosted binary which is a deliberate wedge against bundling but is also extra ops surface for buyers who want a SaaS. (5) No native warehouse-materialisation contract - SageMaker FS, Vertex AI FS, Databricks, and Snowflake all assume offline-in-warehouse + online-in-KV is a first-class pattern with point-in-time correctness; beava is event-driven only. (6) No feature monitoring / drift detection - the hyperscaler bundles all ship distribution sketches, per-feature counters, drift webhooks (Databricks Lakehouse Monitoring, SageMaker Model Monitor, Vertex AI Model Monitoring). (7) No on-demand feature transformations at request time (Tecton/Fennel On-Demand Feature Views, Chalk-style resolvers). (8) No SDK ergonomics for tabular ML idioms returning a DataFrame; bundles ship `get_online_features(entity_rows=DataFrame, ...) -> DataFrame`. (9) No multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs - chargeback-guarantee vendors and T&S platforms hosting many marketplaces cannot isolate them on one beava box. (10) No published recsys-shape (1 user x 200 items x 30 features) batch_get p99 benchmark - the bundle alternatives publish theirs.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo for a self-hostable design-partner play against the bundle; 12mo+ to compete head-on for tier-1 buyers. The procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS + auth + namespace ACLs) are 1-3 months. The hyperscaler-bundle parity gaps (in-process sharding, multi-region replication, warehouse-materialisation, point-in-time correctness contract, get_online_features DataFrame SDK, basic feature monitoring) are 3-9 months on top. A managed/hosted beava offering would be another 6-12 months of GTM and ops work - but is explicitly NOT the wedge against this segment. The wedge IS self-hosted; chasing a managed offering puts beava on the bundle's home turf where it cannot win on price or scale.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Heavily one-sided. Beava-side: zero publicly named users in any of the three referenced use cases under hyperscaler-bundle competitive pressure, no published Databricks-vs-beava or SageMaker-vs-beava bake-off, no DORA/EU Data Act / sovereign-cloud case study citing beava, no design partner in EU fintech or German/French public sector. Repo evidence covering the use case shape: python/beava/demos/fraud/ (18a-shape raw-event ingestion + aggregation), python/beava/demos/ecommerce/ (18b-shape PageView/AddToCart/Purchase), crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json + workloads/fraud.rs are runnable; no marketplace-integrity (10-shape) demo exists yet. The single-binary + Apache-2.0 + ~684k EPS positioning aligns naturally with the buyer who would refuse hyperscaler lock-in, but the public adoption signal is zero in May 2026. Competitor-side validation that the hyperscaler-bundle threat is real: Databricks ~$3.7B ARR / $100B valuation / ~$1.4B Q4-2025 AI run-rate; Tecton acquired at ~$900M with ~$100M ARR; Fennel undisclosed but Rust-engine-acquihire; Featureform -> Redis Feature Form Apr 2026 launch with 'real enterprise hit' reception per SiliconSnark coverage; Snowflake Dynamic Tables 1-minute target lag GA + Online Feature Store layer post-Crunchy; SageMaker FS at Atlassian (10-feature model optimised $425k -> $40k); Vertex AI FS adopted by Wayfair and Shopify. The DORA designation of 19 critical ICT third-party providers on Nov 18 2025 (including AWS/Azure/GCP) and the EU Data Act in force from Sep 12 2025 are the closest thing to a public buyer-side counter-force, but no specific 'we switched off Databricks/SageMaker/Vertex onto an Apache-2.0 self-hosted feature store' case study exists publicly in this segment.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Watch-bordering-on-Compete - the honest framing is uphill. This segment is where category collapse is happening fastest (Tecton + Fennel + Featureform all rolled into bundles inside 6 months Apr-Oct 2025; Redis Feature Form launched Apr 2026) and where beava has the least name recognition. Competing head-on for a tier-1 buyer already standardised on Databricks / Snowflake / SageMaker / Vertex AI / Azure ML is a losing fight on price, integration depth, managed-service polish, and procurement ease. The credible play is the narrow self-hosted Apache-2.0 wedge for sovereign-cloud / EU-data-residency / DORA-concentration-risk / on-prem-fintech / air-gapped buyers - which is a genuine but small slice of the segment. Realistic 12-month outcome: one to three design partners in EU fintech (DORA-driven), one German/French sovereign-cloud-aligned deployment (S3NS / Delos / T-Systems-aligned), one fraud-team at a regulated mid-market buyer who explicitly cannot accept hyperscaler lock-in. Do not pitch this segment as 'we are better than Tecton-now-Databricks' - pitch it as 'we are the option that exists at all if you cannot use them'. Avoid spending engineering effort chasing managed-service parity; double down on the self-hostable + license-clean wedge.
